questions.topic: Type one and type two errors
questions.stem: A debate team fails to reject a false null. Which error is that?

options.text: Type II error, a false negative
Type I error, a false positive
options.misconception: confuses "Type I error, a false positive" with the correct "Type II error, a false negative"

questions.explanation: For a type one and type two errors question like this, the governing rule is: Fail to reject false null = Type II. Applying it makes "Type II error, a false negative" correct. The alternative "No error because null retained" is wrong because it denies false retention.
questions.hint: Fail to reject false null = Type II

questions.learningObjective: Relate power to Type II error
questions.stem: A debate team increases alpha. What happens to power and Type II error?

options.text: Power decreases and Type II error increases
options.misconception: confuses "Power decreases and Type II error increases" with the correct "Power increases and Type II error decreases"

options.text: Power increases and Type II error decreases

options.misconception: names "No change to either" where the rule requires "Power increases and Type II error decreases"
confuses "Both increase" with the correct "Power increases and Type II error decreases"

questions.explanation: Higher alpha increases power and decreases Type II error, trading off Type I. Tradeoff relationship.

questions.stem: A debate team sample mean is 72, population mean 70, SE 2. Compute z-score.
questions.explanation: Applying the z-scores rule — Use (mean-pop mean)/SE — yields "1". Reversing the reasoning would recover the given quantities.

questions.topic: The standard error of a mean
questions.stem: A debate team sample has sd 9 and n=81. Compute the standard error of the mean.
questions.explanation: For a the standard error of a mean question like this, the governing rule is: Divide by sqrt(n). Applying it gives "1" as the answer.
